methodology: Two clocks. The kernel clock is a CUDA graph of one paged_attn_decode launch, replayed with no Python between launches, so the span is device time of the kernel. Bytes are q read plus the output written plus K and V read, for the live tokens only, one layer. GQA does not multiply the KV bytes by the group size. Contexts and the ragged lengths are multiples of the block size, so the last page is full and the mask does not drop slots. Block tables are a seeded shuffle of the pages, which is the paged case; one sequential table is timed at the same bytes to show the shuffle. Five windows, each aimed at 40 ms; the reported time is the median window. The fraction is that GB/s over the median device-to-device copy in bench/results/2026-10-31-m2-bandwidth.json (378.7 GB/s, read plus write, decimal 1e9). The step clock is forward_paged_batch on CUDA bf16, block size 16, the same quantity as bench/profile.py: CUDA events around the forward, then argmax and a per-sequence .item(), after a sync so the card is idle at the start. Five warmup steps, then ten timed steps; seq_len is rewound so every step sees the same context and overwrites the same KV slot. The gather path is the same forward with the decode kernel switched off, so attention gathers pages and the cache write stays the scatter kernel. Tokens/s is batch / median wall seconds. The ceiling uses that same copy bandwidth and decode_step_bytes at the longest row, which is how the M2 table was computed. Host is WSL2. Clocks are not locked. There is no split-KV in this kernel: the grid is (batch, query heads).
